name: James D. Taiclet

career.title: Officer and pilot (aircraft commander, instructor pilot); flew C-141 missions in Operation Desert Shield
President and COO, then CEO (2003) and Chairman (2004)
President and CEO (Chairman since March 2021); board member since January 2018

background_rationale: After Air Force flying and a stint at McKinsey, he ran aerospace services businesses and then led American Tower as an operating CEO for nearly two decades before taking over Lockheed Martin.

notable.summary: Lockheed Martin terminated its planned $4.4 billion acquisition of rocket-engine maker Aerojet Rocketdyne after the FTC sued to block the deal.

Lockheed reported about $1.6 billion in pre-tax program losses in Q2 2025, including $950 million on a classified aeronautics program, with Taiclet saying the company was taking charges to address newly identified risks.
Lockheed received a $35 billion seven-year THAAD procurement award, aimed at sharply increasing interceptor production, alongside a new THAAD munitions facility announced in May 2026.
On a $58.62 billion multiyear PAC-3 MSE award and plans to triple production by 2030, Taiclet said the company was "moving with wartime urgency to deliver the Arsenal of Freedom."

personal_story.hook: A Pittsburgh boilermaker's son, Jim Taiclet flew Lockheed-built C-141 transports in the Air Force before he ran Lockheed.
personal_story.summary: Taiclet was born in Pittsburgh in 1960; his father, an Army veteran, worked as a boilermaker. He went to the U.S. Air Force Academy, graduating in 1982 with degrees in engineering and international relations and captaining the rugby team as a senior, then earned a master's in public affairs at Princeton. As an Air Force pilot he flew Lockheed C-141 Starlifter missions during Operation Desert Shield, and he has said a check-ride instructor taught him that a leader must help the crew finish the job. He moved into business through McKinsey, Pratt & Whitney and Honeywell, spent nearly two decades running American Tower, and joined Lockheed's board in 2018 before becoming CEO in 2020.

quote.context: Recalling an Air Force check ride, in a Boston Magazine interview (July 2017) while American Tower CEO
